themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 200 THIS WEEK—a 256% spike compared to the 56.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72)—signaling a potential infrastructure failure or accelerated deterioration in Tottenville/Great Kills requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 200 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 56.1 weekly average (z-score: 11.72)
Street condition is #3 complaint type overall in 90-day period (1,445 total complaints)
Community board budget requests repeatedly cite need for street reconstruction by DOT
reporting_angles: Ground-truth the specific streets generating complaints—map hotspots and document potholes, flooding, or subsidence
Interview DOT about whether recent weather (snow/ice cleanup) caused damage or if this reflects deferred maintenance

themes_detail.label: Noise from Houses of Worship
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from houses of worship exploded to 4 complaints THIS WEEK—a 3,100% spike from a 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 11.72, high severity)—an unprecedented signal suggesting either a new facility issue, event, or community sensitivity shift.
evidence: 4 noise complaints from houses of worship THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3,100% spike, z-score: 11.72)
This category has historically been near-zero in the district
Suggests either new venue activity, amplified systems, or event concentration this week
reporting_angles: Identify which house(s) of worship were cited in the 4 complaints and what triggered noise (services, events, construction, sound system tests)
Interview both complainants and house of worship leadership to understand what changed this week

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees and Branches
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints spiked to 19 THIS WEEK—a 390% increase from the 3.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.88, high severity)—reflecting either a major weather event stripping branches or deferred forestry maintenance becoming visible.
evidence: 19 overgrown tree/branches complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.9 weekly average (390% spike, z-score: 4.88)
Damaged tree complaints remain steady at 406 total over 90 days, but overgrowth is newly acute
Community board repeatedly requests forestry services and street tree maintenance funding
reporting_angles: Determine if recent snow/ice event caused branch breaks or if this reflects Parks Department backlog in tree trimming
Map complaint locations to see if spike is geographically concentrated or district-wide

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog Incidents
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints surged to 3 complaints THIS WEEK—a 1,100% spike from a 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.35, high severity)—signaling either a new dog or pack problem or heightened resident safety concern in the neighborhood.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Historically near-zero complaint category now showing acute spike
Suggests specific incident(s) or pattern emerging in real time
reporting_angles: Identify the specific locations of the 3 complaints—are they the same dog/area or distributed across district?
Interview affected residents and NYC Parks Enforcement about whether there's a known problematic owner or animal

themes_detail.label: Encampments and Homeless Services Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints (3 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO, z-score: 8.69) and homeless person assistance requests (4 complaints LAST WEEK, z-score: 8.66) show a combined 1,500–2,300% surge, signaling new or growing homelessness in a historically low-incidence district—a potential emerging vulnerability.
evidence: 3 encampment complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (2,300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
4 homeless person assistance complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,500% spike, z-score: 8.66)
Community board budget requests cite need for outreach services to vulnerable populations, suggesting existing concern
reporting_angles: Locate and document the encampment(s)—size, duration, demographics, and what triggered 311 complaints
Interview Department for the Aging and homeless outreach providers about whether they've seen a shift in Tottenville/Great Kills
